steps.what: Read the transcript request from a judge, lawyer or member of the public; confirm the proceeding, requested portion, requester identity and existing release restrictions.
Retrieve the completed authoritative transcript and its revision from {DOCS}; configure native case, date and version fields to avoid repeated folder navigation.

Prepare the requested transcript copy and cover information using native export and page-range settings in the transcript preparation software {OTHER}; preserve exact words, page references and existing required markings.
Check the completed delivery package against the authoritative transcript, request scope, release permissions and recipient; resolve restrictions and approve the final permitted package.
Save the checked final transcript package and request reference in {DOCS}.
Send the exact stored transcript package through the existing authorised delivery channel in the transcript service system {OTHER} to the checked requester.

tasks.design: Configure native transcript indexing in {DOCS} and exact-copy export in the transcript preparation software {OTHER}. The reporter checks access and the completed package before separate save and delivery actions; no model rewrites testimony.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right transcript revision and rebuilding requested copies consumed repeated effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and transcript export presets can reuse explicit case and page-range selections.
tasks.still_hard: A request may concern a restricted proceeding or an ambiguous portion of the record.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve what may be supplied and ensure the package faithfully matches the authoritative record.

ambition.what: No expanded public-access or release authority.

tasks.altitude: Less retrieval and copy preparation; the same release judgement remains.

reach.task: Deliver the correct controlled media version

evidence.claim: Native document metadata and transcript export presets can retrieve and package an existing transcript without generating its words.

assumptions: Boundary is providing an existing completed transcript on request. Creating, correcting and certifying the underlying transcript are separate tasks and gain no second credit here. Shares are illustrative.

The reporter captures case ID, proceeding date, requested portion, requester, recipient channel and release status in s1-s3. Existing record producers supply authoritative transcript ID, revision and page references. Manual lookup and entry remain the fallback; uncertain permission is resolved through the existing process.

Try native indexing and export first. Only repeated navigation and copy assembly lose time. No new approval ceremony or baseline redaction duty is invented; any required restriction handling remains in s1 and s4.

The ordinary completed-package check in s4 binds its exact version and recipient for s5-s6. Edits invalidate both approvals. The reporter's existing release authority and jurisdiction-specific rules remain unchanged.
unknowns: Existing transcript release and delivery requirements
research_questions: Can native export retain authoritative page references for a requested excerpt?

already_counted.description: Check retrieved revision and prepared transcript package.

incremental.description: Maintain metadata and export presets and test controlled delivery references.

approvals.approved_version: Final transcript package checked at the end of s4
Same final package and requester recipient checked at the end of s4, unchanged by s5

tasks.short: Store stenographic symbols and translate them to text

steps.what: Capture the live court proceeding as stenographic symbols using the stenographic recording equipment {OTHER}; enter accurate symbols and record actual speaker and interruption notes while attending to the proceeding.

Use computer-aided transcription software {OTHER} to translate and display the captured symbols as text; configure the reporter's verified case dictionary and native untranslated-symbol view before resolving exceptions.
Check the translated text against the symbol record and permitted source recording, resolve names and ambiguous strokes, and verify the final symbol file and text are complete before storage.
outputs: checked final symbol and text files

steps.what: Save the checked final symbols on computer storage media and the corresponding text file in the computer-aided transcription system {OTHER}.
inputs: checked final symbol and text files

tasks.design: Configure the verified case dictionary and exception views in the existing computer-aided transcription software {OTHER}. Its existing translation runtime earns no labour saving; better dictionary setup reduces repeated exception navigation while the reporter verifies the words and stores the symbols and text.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case terminology and ambiguous strokes were repeatedly located without a configured exception view.
tasks.enabler_now: Native dictionaries and untranslated-symbol views can expose exact mappings and unresolved strokes.
tasks.still_hard: Names, overlapping speech and ambiguous strokes require source-based correction.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve the actual words rather than choosing a plausible sentence.

ambition.what: No automatic transcript certification or delivery.

tasks.altitude: Slightly less translation exception navigation; live capture and textual checking remain.

evidence.claim: Computer-aided stenographic transcription can use verified dictionaries and expose untranslated-symbol exceptions.

assumptions: This is the stenographic court-recording variant of the occupation, not a live caption broadcast. Boundary includes live symbol capture, translation and stored files, not certification or release. Shares are illustrative.

The reporter supplies case ID, session ID, symbol stream, speaker markers and verified name or term mappings during s1-s3. Dictionary entries are checked against actual case materials; missing mappings are resolved manually from permissible sources. Capture and entry time remain counted.

Native dictionary configuration comes first. Only repeated exception lookup in s2 loses time; translation runtime and live attention do not. s1 is the same actual capture action as s2 of task 8655 and uses the shared ID; roll-up must assign it once to recording rather than sum both shares.
The ordinary final file check in s3 covers the exact s4 files. Edits invalidate approval. The original symbol record is preserved and no model invents missing testimony.
unknowns: Permitted recording and file retention arrangements
research_questions: Can native exception views preserve the exact symbol-to-text mapping for review?

already_counted.description: Review dictionary mappings and unresolved translation exceptions.

incremental.description: Maintain and verify case dictionary configuration.

approvals.approved_version: Final symbol and translated-text file snapshots checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Exception navigation reduces 25% of the 20-hour translation-handling share: 5 gross hours less 1 upkeep. Zero with native views already used. Live capture, source correction and save retain full time; shared capture is counted once in roll-up.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record court and assembly proceedings verbatim

steps.what: Set up and test computerized or stenographic recording equipment {OTHER} for the court or assembly session; configure native session presets for the existing input and storage settings while personally checking speakers and signal capture.

Capture the live court proceeding as stenographic symbols using the stenographic recording equipment {OTHER}; enter accurate symbols and record actual speaker and interruption notes while attending to the proceeding.
Check the captured session's continuity, speaker markers and actual interruption notes; record gaps and verify the final raw recording package against the session log.
Save the checked final raw session package in the recording system {OTHER} under the correct case and session references.

tasks.design: Reuse native session presets in the recording equipment {OTHER} while retaining the reporter's equipment test and uninterrupted verbatim capture. The reporter checks the actual raw session package before its separate save; later text translation is a distinct task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Session input and storage settings were repeatedly entered despite stable equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: Native session presets can restore explicit settings without replacing the capture test.
tasks.still_hard: Overlapping speech, unexpected speakers and equipment faults require the reporter's immediate attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a capture gap while the speaker can still clarify it.
tasks.altitude: A small setup saving; the reporter remains present throughout the proceeding.

evidence.claim: Recording equipment can reuse session settings while requiring an actual input and capture test.

assumptions: One court-session stenographic instance is modelled; assemblies and stenomask variants need their own equipment checks. Boundary ends at the raw session package, not translated or certified text. Shares are illustrative.

The reporter supplies case ID, session ID, input selection, storage destination and actual test result in s1, then produces speaker markers and actual interruption notes during s2. Missing details are entered manually; no session completion is inferred from the calendar.

Native presets are tested first. Savings are repeated settings only, not live recording duration, machine runtime or post-session checking. s2 is exactly the capture action in task 8663 s1; its shared ID requires one owner in roll-up.
The ordinary final raw-package check at s3 approves the exact s4 package. Changes invalidate it. This storage action is distinct from task 8663's final corrected symbol-and-text files.
unknowns: Current raw package retention and backup process
research_questions: Can a native preset restore settings while making the actual test result visible?

already_counted.description: Check restored session settings and perform the equipment test.

incremental.description: Verify presets after equipment or storage changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final raw session package checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native presets remove 20% of the 10-hour setup share: 2 gross hours less 0.5 upkeep. Zero if already configured. Live capture and record checking retain full time; shared capture is counted once in roll-up.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare the attorney-requested deposition's session references and recording equipment {OTHER}; use native session presets while checking participants, inputs and actual capture quality.
Record the deposition or other attorney-requested proceeding, track speakers and actual interruptions, and address unclear speech through the established reporting procedure.
Check the completed deposition recording, continuity, participant references and actual interruption notes; resolve or document gaps and check the final recording package.
Save the checked final deposition recording package in the recording system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native deposition session presets in the recording system {OTHER}. The reporter still verifies participants and equipment, records the actual proceeding and checks the final package before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated session settings consumed preparation time for otherwise similar deposition setups.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presets can reuse input and record-reference defaults without assuming the session was captured successfully.
tasks.still_hard: Remote participants, overlapping speech and confidential content require attentive reporting.
tasks.human_edge: Ensure the live record reflects the actual proceeding and make unresolved gaps explicit.

ambition.what: No automatic certification or attorney delivery.

tasks.altitude: Slightly less preparation; recording duties and existing authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native recording session presets can reuse explicit setup fields while keeping actual recording tests human.

assumptions: This is a distinct attorney-requested deposition, not the same court session in tasks 8655 and 8663. Boundary is raw recording through storage; transcript creation and delivery are separate. Shares are an illustrative scenario.

The reporter captures deposition ID, date, participant references, input selection, storage destination and actual test result in s1, with actual speaker and interruption notes in s2. Manual entry and test work are retained. No session is marked recorded from a booking.
Native presets come first. Only repeated settings lose time; participant confirmation, equipment test, live attention and final checking remain. No new report or approval ceremony is introduced.
The normal final package check in s3 binds the exact s4 recording. Edits invalidate approval. This raw-record storage does not certify or send a transcript.
research_questions: Can session defaults be reused without copying prior participant or case identifiers incorrectly?

already_counted.description: Verify deposition setup and actual capture test.

incremental.description: Maintain and check session presets after equipment changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final deposition recording package checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Preset reuse removes 20% of the 15-hour preparation share: 3 gross hours less 0.5 upkeep. Zero if presets are already used. Live recording, actual notes, final check and save retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The reporter retains verbatim capture and release responsibilities, with modest native setup gains and larger retrieval gains only where current tools are underused.
reach: Work with sound engineering technicians on input quality and continuity
role.ambitious_version: Provide a traceable verbatim record with explicit gaps and controlled delivery, preserving the reporter's responsibility for actual words.
